questions.question: Datasets A (45, 48, 50, 52, 55) and B (20, 35, 50, 65, 80) both have mean 50. Their ranges are:
The main weakness of the range is that it:
options: Requires the data to be ordered twice
Cannot be computed for even datasets
Uses only the two extreme values, so one outlier distorts it completely
Is always larger than the mean

questions.question: A complete statistical summary of a dataset should report:
options: A measure of centre AND a measure of spread

questions.question: For the ordered sales data 4, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18, 20, 25, the median is:
The lower and upper quartiles of that data are:
options: Q_1 = 8; Q_3 = 18 — the medians of the lower and upper halves

questions.question: The interquartile range and semi-interquartile range are:
The IQR is preferred over the range when outliers are present because the IQR:
options: Measures the spread of the middle half, which extreme values cannot touch
Uses every value in the dataset

subtopics.title: The Five-Number Summary and the Box-and-Whisker Diagram

questions.question: The five-number summary of the sales data is:
In a box-and-whisker diagram, the box itself runs:
options: From the minimum to the maximum
From Q_1 to Q_3, with a line inside at the median
From the median to the maximum

questions.question: Each of the four sections of a box plot (two whiskers, two box halves) contains:
options: An amount of data proportional to its length
About a quarter of the data, regardless of the section's length

questions.question: A very LONG whisker means that quarter of the data is:
options: Larger in count than the other quarters
Spread over a wide stretch of values

subtopics.title: Percentiles, Skew and Comparing Two Box Plots

questions.question: The upper quartile is the same value as the:
A box plot with the median close to Q_1 and a long upper whisker shows data that is:
options: Skewed to the right (positively skewed) — bunched low with a tail of large values

questions.question: Class A: median 60, IQR 12. Class B: median 55, IQR 30. The correct two-sentence comparison is:
options: A scored lower and was less consistent
A typically scored higher, and A was more consistent because its middle half is less spread out
B typically scored higher, and B was more consistent

questions.question: Scoring at the 90th percentile of a test means:
options: You scored 90 percent on the paper
You beat 10 percent of the candidates
About 90 percent of candidates scored below your mark
Your mark was 90 minus the median

questions.question: Two taxi routes both average 30 minutes, but route one's trips span 28-32 minutes and route two's span 15-45. The averages hide:
options: The spread — route two's trips wander far more from the centre

questions.question: The ranges of the two routes are:
options: Route one: 4 minutes; route two: 30 minutes

questions.question: In everyday terms, a small spread in trip times means the service is:
options: Reliable — you can predict your arrival time

subtopics.title: Folding the Line in Half, Then in Half Again

questions.question: In the folding picture, the quartiles are found by taking:
options: Every third person in the line
The two people at the ends
The middle of the whole line, then the middle of each half

questions.question: With eleven values, the person holding the median:
options: Belongs to neither half — the middle value is the fence, not a resident

questions.question: The wild days of 4 and 25 sandwiches cannot stretch the IQR because:
options: The IQR is measured between the two quartile fences, and extremes sit outside them
The IQR uses only the median

questions.question: For summary 4; 8; 13; 18; 25, the box's two walls stand at:
'Long never means many' is a reminder that a long section of a box plot holds:
options: More data points than a short section
The same quarter of the data, spread over a wider stretch of values

questions.question: When comparing two box plots, a full-marks comparison must mention:
options: The centres (medians) AND the spreads (box lengths or IQRs)
